title: In-plane optimal qubit operation with control fidelities exceeding 99 %
authors: Yu-Chen Zhou, Zhenzhen Kong, Rong-Long Ma, Hao-Tian Jiang, Ao-Ran Li, Yang Zhong, Zhi-Tao Wu, Rui Zheng, Gui-Lei Wang, Gang Cao, Hai-Ou Li, Guo-Ping Guo
abstract: Hole spin qubits based on semiconductor quantum dots are promising for building future large-scale quantum computers owing to their all-electrical manipulation. However, abundant physical mechanisms of valence band holes lead to anisotropic qubit properties. There is an opportunity to prolong the coherence time and achieve high-fidelity qubit manipulations. Here, we report a single-hole spin qubit in a planar germanium quantum dot and investigate its anisotropic susceptibility to charge noise under an in-plane magnetic field. By correlating the longitudinal spin-electric susceptibility with qubit coherence and control performance, we identify an optimal operating point where the sensitivity to charge noise is minimized. We find that optimizing the magnetic-field orientation reduces the spin-electric susceptibility, resulting in a five-fold enhancement of the Hahn-echo coherence time and a nearly tenfold suppression of control infidelity. At the optimal operating point, gate set tomography demonstrates the maximum gate fidelity of 99.82 %. Our finding enhances the prospects of hole spin qubits for scalable quantum information processing.
summary: This paper reports on optimizing hole spin qubits in germanium quantum dots by tuning the in-plane magnetic field orientation. The authors found that minimizing the qubit's susceptibility to charge noise significantly enhances coherence times and gate fidelity. This work advances the feasibility of using hole spin qubits for scalable quantum computation.
main_problem: The primary goal is to improve the coherence time and control fidelity of hole spin qubits, which are susceptible to charge noise due to their physical mechanisms.
main_result: By optimizing the orientation of the in-plane magnetic field, the authors achieved a five-fold enhancement in Hahn-echo coherence time and demonstrated a maximum gate fidelity of 99.82%.
method: The study involves measuring the anisotropic spin-electric susceptibility to charge noise while varying the magnetic field orientation and performing gate set tomography.
model_or_system: The research uses hole spin qubits realized in planar germanium quantum dots (DQD). The system's properties are highly dependent on the orientation of an applied in-plane magnetic field and gate voltages.
key_observables: Longitudinal spin-electric susceptibility (LSES), Hahn-echo coherence time (T_Echo^2), and maximum gate fidelity.
important_parameters: In-plane magnetic field orientation ($	heta_{xy}$), charge noise sensitivity, and gate fidelity (e.g., 99.82%).
main_assumptions: The coherence time limitation is directly correlated with the minimization of the spin-electric susceptibility, suggesting charge noise is the dominant decoherence source.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the anisotropy of effective g-factors and the angular dependence of LSES, T_Echo^2, and the resulting quality factors (Q*) for the two qubits (Q1 and Q2).
paper_structure: The paper systematically investigates the angular dependence of qubit parameters, linking the minimization of charge noise susceptibility (LSES) to the maximization of coherence time and gate fidelity.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete experimental evidence for mitigating charge noise effects in solid-state spin qubits by engineering the magnetic field orientation, which is crucial for scaling quantum processors.
